revised_question: What is Avashyaka and how is it understood in Jain teachings?
revised_answer: The concept of Avashyaka is central to Jain spiritual practice. According to Aavashyak Sutra (AGAM-028), the text explains: "sacitta phala-sabjI kA tyAga parivAra kA tyAga karemi bhaMte! sAmAiyaM savvaM sAvajjaM jogaM paccakkhAmi jAvajjIvAe, tivihaM tiviheNaM maNeNaM, bAyAe, ka karemi, na kAravemi, karatapi annaM na samajANA khetIbAr3I kA tyAga dhana-sonA-cA~dIAdi kA tyAga tassa bhaMte paDikkamA niMdAmi garihAmi a bosirAmi jIvana paryaMta kAryoM ke kI" This commentary was prepared by Amarmuni.

revised_question: What is Samayik and how is it understood in Jain teachings?
revised_answer: The concept of Samayik is central to Jain spiritual practice. According to Uttaradhyayana Sutra (AGAM-030), the text explains: "uttarAdhyayana sUtra. adhyAtma kAvya uttarAdhyayana sUtra kA viSaya atyadhika vizAla, evaM jIvanavyApI hai| yaha eka adhyAtma kAvya hai, to nIti, dharma, AcAra evaM itihAsa kA bhI mahAna grantha hai| karmavijJAna, manovijJAna, jIvavijJAna, aura vanaspativijJAna Adi aneka viSayoM kA sundara yuktipUrNa vivecana isameM milatA hai| bhagavAna mahAvIra kI antima vANI ke rUpa meM sampUrNa jaina jagata meM isakI viziSTa mAnyatA evaM zraddhA hai| uttarAdhyayana ke niyamita svAdhyAya pATha kI vizeSa param" This commentary was prepared by Amarmuni.
